text:
Ada: Quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC — I'm worried about the perf / complexity split if we move full tenant access checks into the query executor vs keeping them in the console layer. Thoughts?
Jon: I'd prefer query-layer checks for strong isolation, but that forces us to carry policy logic through the query planner which is messy. Also harder to reuse across dashboards.
Keven: Agreed with Jon on reuse. Practical tradeoff: do lightweight filtering in the query layer (deny-by-default predicates), and do richer shape/feature gating in the console. That keeps hot-path checks cheap.
Lucy: Are we sure lightweight predicates won't blow up index selection? If we add a bunch of dynamic predicates per-tenant we could regress p99. We should benchmark with 100k tenant rules.
Ada: Good point. Proposal: 1) push a canonical "tenant_id" predicate into the executor (indexed path), 2) surface feature gates (columns/views toggles) in console, and 3) if feature gating is complex, compile it down to a pre-filter job that populates a temporary allow-list cache.
Jon: I like the allow-list cache idea. Suggest TTL + versioning so rollouts don't need global invalidation. Simple API: /cache/allowlist/<tenant>/<feature>?version=42
Keven: Implementation note: pre-filter job can run as async materialization on the cluster, keyed by (tenant, feature_version). That avoids per-request compute but introduces staleness; we should define staleness SLO.
Lucy: For SLOs: aim for eventual consistency within 30s for feature flips, 1s for tenant-deny changes. Tenant-deny must be near-real-time for security-sensitive flows.
Ada: Ok — security-sensitive rules will always be sync and enforced in query executor. Everything else can be async.
Keven: Rollout plan: Canary on dedicated infra (10 tenants), measure p50/p95/p99 for common dashboard queries. If p99 regresses >15% we abort.
Ada: Can we add an executor metric for "predicate-cost-estimate" so we can signal when tenant predicates are making queries pick bad plans?
Jon: Yes. We'll add histograms: executor.predicate_eval_time_ms and executor.plan_repick_count. Dashboard team can alert on plan_repick_count spikes.
Lucy: Edge case: cross-tenant shared tiles (cache entries used by multiple tenants). If we keep tenant predicates in executor, those tiles won't be shared and cache hit rate drops. Need a hybrid: tile keys include feature_version fingerprint so safe sharing is possible when rules identical.
Ada: Good call. Add fingerprinting to tile key: sha256(tenant_policy_fingerprint || feature_version) so identical policies share tiles.
Keven: Also recommend a fallback for capacity constraints: if executor is overloaded, let console route low-priority dashboards to a degraded path that uses precomputed aggregates. That keeps SLAs for interactive users.
Jon: Can we implement degraded path as a per-route policy in the routing table? i.e., route.priorities = [fast, degraded, background] and fallthrough rules.
Lucy: Yes, route-level config + an operator flag to enable emergency degrade across clusters.
deploy-bot: CI: prefilter-materialization e2e tests passed (build #3421) :white_check_mark:
Ada: Next actions: write short RFC addendum with: predicate split, allow-list cache API + TTL, tile-fingerprinting, metric names, and canary checklist. I'll author and ping for review.
Jon: Happy to review — will scope perf test harness.
Keven: I'll prototype the prefilter materializer job this week.
Lucy: I'll draft SLO language and alerting rules.
Ada: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
